title: Glasshouse — institutional accountability evidence dataset (say vs. do)
description:
Glasshouse is a public, machine-readable record of what large asset managers say about how they vote their funds' shares (archived proxy-voting and stewardship policies, with dates) and how those funds actually voted (SEC Form N-PX), with 13-F holdings and a public enforcement record alongside.

This version holds 16,742,083 fund vote lines from meetings between 1 July 2023 and 30 June 2026, filed by fund trusts of 22 financial institutions. For 19 of them (BlackRock, Vanguard, State Street, Fidelity, Dimensional, Nuveen/TIAA, Capital Group, Columbia Threadneedle, Wellington, Parametric, J.P. Morgan, Goldman Sachs, BNY, Invesco, T. Rowe Price, Franklin Templeton, DWS, Northern Trust, Charles Schwab) every kind of vote is on file for the fund trusts held; for UBS, BNP Paribas and Bank of America only executive-pay (say-on-pay) votes are on file. The fund trusts held are often a small part of a large manager: this is not a complete record of any manager's voting. Some 2025–2026 Dimensional N-PX exhibits contain exactly 500,000 proxy records in the SEC file itself and appear capped, so their counts are lower bounds. It also holds 98 dated versions of 20 managers' policy documents (hashes, dates and archive links; no policy text), 580,106 13-F holding rows and 14,887 enforcement actions.

New in this version: Nuveen/TIAA (6 trusts), Columbia Threadneedle (6 trusts) and Parametric (6 Eaton Vance series it votes as sub-adviser). 19 policy versions now come from fund statements of additional information (SAIs) on EDGAR that print the voting policy, dated by the filing date (labels ending '-as-printed-in-sai'); they give dated policy text back to 2023 for Geode, Wellington, Parametric, Columbia and Nuveen. Where a fund's SAI switched to a different policy (Parametric series to the Morgan Stanley policy in 2026), later votes carry their own key and are never paired with the earlier text.

Votes are attributed to the adviser that cast them, not the brand: where one group's funds are voted by different advisers under different policies (BlackRock, Vanguard, T. Rowe Price, DWS) every vote carries an adviser_key, and a policy may only be compared with votes of the same key. Three derived tables give one row per manager per ballot item (shareholder proposals, director elections, say-on-pay). Every column and code is defined in DATASHEET.md; coverage and known gaps are stated in COVERAGE.json; every file is checksummed in MANIFEST.sha256.

Code: https://github.com/glasshouse-records/promises-kept-or-not (MIT). The DATASHEET records the exact code commit that built these files.

The dataset records facts from public filings. It makes no finding of wrongdoing about anyone.
notes: Code: MIT. Data: CC-BY-4.0. Built from code commit recorded in DATASHEET.md.
